transcript.text: Thank you all for being here. As you know, we have a ninth-grade student returning after missing four days due to a concussion, and I need to approve a re-entry plan for the next two school weeks. I've reviewed the draft plan, which keeps the student on the full daily schedule, permits ordinary PE participation, allows up to three make-up assignments per day, and schedules an in-person counselor check-in after school. Before I approve anything, I want to hear from each of you. Nurse, teachers, counselor -- is there anything I should know that might change this draft plan? Please share any concerns or information you have.

transcript.text: Mr. Bennett, I need to share something important. Over the last two days, I've observed in my science classroom that this student develops headache symptoms after completing more than one make-up assignment in a single day. I recorded this in my own lesson notes, but I haven't yet added it to the shared plan. Based on this, I believe my science class should assign no more than one make-up assignment per day during the re-entry period. This suggests the draft plan's allowance of up to three make-up assignments per day may be too much for this student.

transcript.text: Mr. Bennett, I need to share critical information from the physician's return-to-school note that I reviewed this morning. It was faxed to my office but has not yet been entered into the student-information system. The physician's note explicitly prohibits physical education and contact sports for exactly 10 school days, and it requires a 20-minute rest break after lunch during that same period. This directly conflicts with the draft plan, which permits ordinary PE participation and does not include any rest break after lunch. The draft plan must be revised to remove PE for the next 10 school days and to build in a 20-minute rest period after lunch.
